request.system: You are clustering code review findings from one PR. Always respond with valid JSON.
request.prompt:
You are clustering code review findings from the same PR. For each PAIR below, decide whether the two findings describe the SAME underlying issue — same root cause in the same code location. Different wording is fine. A finding about a DIFFERENT defect in the same file or function is NOT the same issue. Severity or aspect differences of the same root cause ARE the same issue.


For THIS scoring pass, duplicate equivalence is stricter than sharing a root cause.
You must compare the COMPLETE MATERIAL CLAIMS, including mechanism, triggering
conditions, execution path, and consequence. The same line or broad concern does
not establish equivalence. A report of wrong-category selection, a case/rename
mismatch, a crash, and a silent fallback are different claims even at one lookup.
An inactive/unbound API concern and an alleged active user-facing failure differ.
A compound report with an additional material claim does NOT equal its subset.
Differences only in wording, severity, or hedging do not create separate claims.
If the claimed mechanisms, triggers or consequences conflict, or one report adds
an unsupported/different material factual claim, return same=false. You are NOT
verifying which claim is true; do not repair or reinterpret either report to make
them match. If unsure whether their full claims are equivalent, return false.

For every numbered pair, extract what A and B actually CLAIM into mechanism,
trigger and consequence. Then list material_differences and give your equivalence
verdict, confidence and reason. same=true requires no material differences.
Return ONLY this JSON object, with EVERY pair index exactly once:
{"pairs":[{"pair":1,"a":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"b":{"mechanism":"...","trigger":"...","consequence":"..."},"material_differences":[],"same":true,"confidence":0.9,"reason":"..."}]}

PAIRS:
PAIR 1:
A: The credential DB-fetch copied into handleCancelBooking omits the `app: { select: { slug: true } }` include and the appName remapping that the identical blocks in EventManager perform, handing getCalendar a credential with no appName. Cancelling a collective booking whose calendar reference points at a teammate's credential (never present in bookingToDelete.user.credentials) fetches a credential that cannot be resolved to an integration the way the EventManager copies arrange, so `calendar?.deleteEvent` silently no-ops and the teammate's calendar keeps the cancelled event.
B: The DB fallback fetches the credential with prisma.credential.findUnique and no app include or appName mapping, unlike the parallel EventManager code that maps appName from app.slug before calling getCalendar. For team hosts whose credential is not in the organizer's user.credentials — exactly the collective case this PR targets — getCalendar receives a credential with no app identity, cannot resolve the calendar app, returns null, and calendar?.deleteEvent silently no-ops, leaving those hosts' events on their calendars after cancellation.

B: handleCancelBooking DB credential fallback is a silent no-op — the raw credential is fetched without including the app relation or mapping appName, so getCalendar (which dispatches on credential.appName) returns null and deleteEvent never runs, leaving orphaned calendar events on hosts' calendars

PAIR 3:

On installs with team billing disabled, organization create persists no slug at all (org slug lookups/URLs fail, or Prisma rejects the create if slug is required); on billing-enabled installs the slug is now set at creation time, defeating the requestedSlug/isOrganizationVerified=false verification flow that the very next line still implements.
B: The slug condition was silently inverted from `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` — an unrelated behavior change smuggled into a destinationCalendar PR with no acceptance. With IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false, Organization.create runs without the required unique slug and the insert fails, breaking organization creation entirely; with it true, unverified organizations immediately occupy their slug, bypassing the requestedSlug verification flow the adjacent line (153) still implements.

B: N+1 DB queries and fully sequential event creation in createAllCalendarEvents: per-destination loop issues prisma.credential.findUnique and awaits createEvent serially, scaling latency linearly with host count; same shape duplicated in updateAllCalendarEvents (~lines 493-540)

B: Same N+1 pattern in updateAllCalendarEvents: sequential await of prisma.credential.findUnique per calendar reference serializes the loop head even though updateEvent promises are fired concurrently; batch-fetch credentials up front

PAIR 9:
A: CalendarEvent.schedulingType is added to the public type and set on evt here, but nothing anywhere in the changeset ever reads it. The field is dead payload crossing the CalendarEvent boundary and its SchedulingType import widens the public type surface for no consumer, so the next reader must guess whether COLLECTIVE-only semantics were intended and the addition is untraceable to any requirement in this PR.
B: `schedulingType: eventType.schedulingType` is added to the CalendarEvent payload and a SchedulingType field added to the CalendarEvent interface, but no code in this diff ever reads evt.schedulingType. Ships-inert API surface: a payload field crossing into every calendar/email path with no consumer, inviting future readers to assume it drives behavior it does not; the isTeamEventType && COLLECTIVE check is done inline at push time instead.

PAIR 10:
A: CalendarEvent.schedulingType is added to the public type and set on evt here, but nothing anywhere in the changeset ever reads it. The field is dead payload crossing the CalendarEvent boundary and its SchedulingType import widens the public type surface for no consumer, so the next reader must guess whether COLLECTIVE-only semantics were intended and the addition is untraceable to any requirement in this PR.
B: `schedulingType?: SchedulingType | null` is added to the shared CalendarEvent contract and populated on every booking in handleNewBooking, but nothing in this diff ever reads it. Ships-inert surface on the core event type: every future CalendarEvent producer must decide what to populate there, and readers may assume it is meaningful when no consumer defines its contract.

PAIR 11:
A: createAllCalendarEvents now awaits createEvent sequentially per destination inside the for-loop, where the previous code created events concurrently via Promise.all for the multi-credential path. A collective booking with N hosts serializes N calendar API round-trips on the booking request path, adding roughly (N-1) × per-call latency (hundreds of ms each) to every collective booking confirmation for the booker waiting on the response.
B: createAllCalendarEvents now awaits each destination's calendar creation (plus a possible per-destination credential DB fetch) sequentially in a for-loop, while the sibling no-credentialId branch still uses Promise.all. Booking-creation latency for collective events grows linearly with host count — a 5-host collective serializes 5 calendar API calls plus any DB fetches on the hot booking path, adding multiple seconds that parallel creation (as the adjacent branch already does) would avoid.

PAIR 12:
A: The COLLECTIVE gate is written as the raw string literal 'COLLECTIVE' (here and again at line 1071) although the same file previously used the SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE enum. The discriminator that turns the entire multi-host feature on is no longer compile-checked, so a future enum rename or new scheduling variant silently stops matching here and collective bookings revert to single-calendar behavior.
B: The diff replaces the SchedulingType.COLLECTIVE / SchedulingType.ROUND_ROBIN enum comparisons with bare string literals ("COLLECTIVE", "ROUND_ROBIN"), repeated at three sites (~689, ~988, ~1077) instead of a named typed constant. A typo or enum-value rename no longer fails compilation — a misspelled literal in the includes() array silently evaluates false, flipping isTeamEventType and the collective destination-calendar behavior with none of the compile-check protection the previous enum constants provided.
